Comparing Utpal Sanghvi, Jamnabai Narsee School, Podar, and Maneckji Cooper often comes up when people talk about academics in Mumbai. All four schools are well known and have been around for a long time, which gives them a certain fixed structure.

From the outside, they share a similar image of disciplined routines, packed timetables, and a strong focus on exams that shapes how students move through their school years. In conversations about schools in Juhu, the differences are usually described in terms of classroom environment rather than academic labels.

Some are seen as more strict, others as slightly more flexible, but the core experience still revolves around textbooks, tests, and coaching classes after school. While reading through online discussions, I noticed Billabong High International School mentioned once during a broader comparison, without much explanation, simply as another familiar name people recognize in the area. What tends to stand out is how similar student life sounds across these schools. Long school hours, regular assessments, tuition outside school, and pressure around board exams come up repeatedly. Teachers change, batches change, but the overall academic rhythm stays steady year after year, shaping how students spend most of their time during school.

From an educational point of view, comparing these schools often feels more abstract than practical. On paper, they overlap a lot in curriculum and expectations. In real life, the experience seems to depend more on individual teachers, peer groups, and how a student adapts to the routine, rather than the name printed on the school uniform.

The general assumption has been that playschools are just fun and games and children are sent to a playschool just for a change in environment while parents consider those 2 -3 hours as me time. However, overtime I have realised that playschools play a very important role in the growth of a child. I read that children make the maximum synaptic connections till the age of 8 years, so as per research, this is a crucial period of children.

This is why I have always recommended to friends and family to pay serious attention to playschool while looking at overall education for your children. This is the first time in their lives that they will interact with strangers and go to a new environment.

To select a good playschool you can look at mass or premium preschools. The mass ones are at a lower fee structure and have basic facilities. Howeber the premium ones are playschools that value personalised learning, introduce many activities at a young age and pay strict attention to safety.

Some of the premium playschools in Mumbai are:

Safari Kid: International Preschool, Kindergarten & Day Care | Safari Kid International

Maple Bear: International Play School India, Preschool Education, Bear Care India

Kangaroo Kids: Best Preschool, Play School, Nursery, Kindergarten & Montessori School in India

The preschool is ISO certified in terms of safety as this was one of my major concerns while selecting the playschool. Also they make sure parents play an important part in the child’s learning process and invite us to many child-bonding activities, they also invite our parents i.e their grandparents on different occasions. My parents too were surprised to see the change in my children. As a parent I value preschool learning more today as I have also learnt to teach my child differently. There are many preschools in different parts of Mumbai

- The location should be close to home or office.

- Certified teachers especially for handling toddlers.

- The play area should be safe for kids even if teachers or nannies are not watching them.

- Hygienic and spacious for our kid to feel comfortable.

- New age learning for our kid.

- Good curriculum and reporting system.

We also have a WhatsApp group of all the parents in the same class. So, we get to know all the updates of what all the other kids are doing. We are really glad that we made the list and didn't have to compromise on any of it. If you ask us we will definitely say it Eager Beavers.

If you’re looking for one of the top international preschools in Mumbai, Nahar International School (NIS) in Chandivali / Powai is a very strong choice. Here’s a concise overview of what makes it stand out:

NIS offers a dedicated Early Years programme (EYFS 1 – Nursery, EYFS 2 – Junior KG, EYFS 3 – Senior KG) under its “Bees & Cubs” preschool wing.
The preschool programme is built on the Cambridge Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) guidelines, blending play-based, enquiry-based learning with structure as children grow.
NIS is part of a full K-12 international school, offering Cambridge Primary, IGCSE, IB DP and A-Levels. This means continuity from the preschool years into higher grades.
Infrastructure is modern and child-friendly: labs, library, auditorium, large playgrounds, free play spaces and so on.
The admission policy is transparent: For pre-primary they accept children from age 3 in the term they turn three.
Visit during class time to observe how the preschool teachers engage with children in the “Bees & Cubs” programme. Are children comfortably exploring, interacting and engaged in creative play?
Inspect the outdoor/play area: according to their site it includes a turf ground and free-play zones. Physical activity is important in early years.
Ask about teacher-child ratio: their admissions policy mentions “Pre Primary Section teacher/student ratio 2:24”.
Review curriculum progression: Although preschool is play-based, the school emphasises preparing children for primary schooling—so check how literacy and numeracy are introduced.
Ask about fees, availability of seat in the year, transport (if needed) and sibling policy.
If you’re living in or near Andheri East / Powai / Chandivali, it’s very convenient.
